places.name: La Coruña
past: The old village of Myrithi: farms about a green, with a little church, beside the road.
Raised as a tower keep on the rise above the meeting of the roads; a hamlet gathered beneath its walls. The old village kept its own church, outside the town’s bounds.
Walled.
A great fire burned 21 houses; it was rebuilt in stone.
A great fire burned 10 houses; it was rebuilt in stone.
The old village of Myrithi was at last taken within the walls.
The town outgrew its walls. The new circuit keeps 82% of the old wall and runs out only where the suburbs had spread; a stretch of the old wall inside was pulled down for a street along its line.
The walls were rebuilt on the new trace: earthen ramparts faced in stone, angled bastions and a ditch; 13 houses outside were cleared for the glacis.
A citadel was raised astride the walls on the western side; 21 houses of the old quarter were razed for it and its glacis, and a garrison quartered there for good.
The old tower keep was rebuilt as a great castle on the same ground.
The parish church was pulled down and rebuilt on its own ground as a great minster.

places.name: Puerto Luna
past: The bishop's cathedral and its burg stood on the dry rise; below, the count founded a merchants' town on the waterfront. For a generation they had two councils, then one. Canals — fleets — were dug from the harbour into the merchant quarter, so that lighters could unload at the warehouse doors.
Walled.

captain.office: warden of The brewers of Puerto Luna

places.name: Puente de la Cuervo
past: The old village of Westerheim: farms about a green, with a little church, beside the road.
A hamlet grew up at the ford where the road crosses the river; a bridge replaced the ford in its second age. The old village kept its own church, outside the town’s bounds.
The ford was bridged in stone.
Walled.

places.name: A Pescadería
past: Founded in Roman times about a forum. Parts of the ancient street grid survive in the core; medieval lanes and subdivided plots grew around them.
A great fire burned 17 houses; it was rebuilt in stone.
Besieged; the suburbs outside the gates were burned to deny the enemy cover, and grew back after the peace.
A new parish church was built for the growing quarter.
The walls were rebuilt on the new trace: earthen ramparts faced in stone, angled bastions and a ditch; 32 houses outside were cleared for the glacis.
A citadel was raised astride the walls on the southern side; 24 houses of the old quarter were razed for it and its glacis, and a garrison quartered there for good.
A great fire burned 15 houses; it was rebuilt in stone.

captain.name: Clara Costa
captain.office: warden of The carpenters of A Pescadería

places.name: Elviña
past: An older settlement grew into a town in Roman times. Its main routes survive, with irregular medieval lanes and plots shaped by the ground.
Granted a charter for a weekly market; the green was paved as a market place.
Walled.

captain.office: warden of The tailors of Elviña
